status: Unapproved specification data. Expected results were written by hand from the draft. The reference checker and models in ldrcore/ run them, which shows that they agree with code by the same author and nothing more; no relay or client exists.
author: Fable (claude seat), for cross-review by Codex

coverage.checked_by: A structural lint, and since draft v6 the reference checker in ldrcore/ for apply vectors (not traces). The lint checks: identifiers unique and sequential, fixtures resolve, premises declared, reasons and types from the declared sets, these counts correct. The lint computes no outcome and establishes none. Codex's static review of the first 95 vectors and 29 traces is docs/LDR-CONFORMANCE-REVIEW.md; it did not execute anything either.
coverage.reviewed_statically: Codex also read A105-A125 and T03, T16, T27, T32, T33, T37 statically (call 0002 turn 16), then A126-A130 and T38 (turn 18). A131-A145 and T39 are newer than any review. A174-A211 and T40-T42 (draft v7) have not been reviewed by anyone. T43-T47 follow Codex's independent probe of the client model (call 0003, turns 11 and 13): Codex read the texts of T43-T47 as they stood at 7b79dd2 and asked for no change (turn 15); it ran TestClientTraces at that commit. T47 then gained a step about a stopped credential's anchor request; Codex ran the traces again at af39840 and accepted T47's wording (turn 17). The expectations of T11 and T40 about a revoked key's anchor request changed with the same review.
coverage.executed: ldrcore/apply_test.go runs every active apply vector. A134-A145 were added after a mutation check of that package showed eleven rules that no earlier vector pinned; their expected results were still written from the draft, not copied from the implementation. A146-A162 follow Codex's independent run of the checker (docs/LDR-CHECKER-REVIEW.md), which found three behaviours no vector covered: an oversize turn committed, a record other than line_init committed on an empty log, and a subset committed as the default audience. A163-A173 follow its second probe, which showed counters wrapping at the top of their range. A174-A211 came with draft v7, which follows Codex's enrollment, bootstrap and envelope draft v1: A174-A194 cover a credential's two keys, the key registry across roles, operator-key tombstones, a line_init without a root key, and a disabled actor that cannot be moved; A195-A211 pin that an absent required expectation is malformed, one vector per required expectation. Draft v7 also changed vectors that already existed, because the rules changed: enrollment records and credential state carry two keys and a request digest (A77-A79, A130, A135, A136, A158, A159, A167 and the fixtures), line_init names a root key (A122, A123), a revoked operator key leaves a tombstone (A120's resulting state, A124's starting state), and A135 and A136 were restated for derived identifiers. No expected outcome changed.
coverage.not_covered: recovery_generation has no apply vector: its effect is a rebuild from a base, not a patch. It appears in traces T15 and T28 only. Root and bootstrap coverage (A116-A123) is a handful of semantic cases, not a complete suite, and models no cryptographic proof.
coverage.traces_are: Reviewable scenarios in prose with symbolic intents and often without explicit times. They are not executable inputs. Each trace has a run label saying whether a Go test in ldrcore/ re-enacts it with explicit inputs: 27 against the sequencer model, 13 against the client model, 4 against the register model, and 3 as a sequence of Apply calls only.

conventions.state: Semantic state of the draft's sections 6.1, 7.1 and 8, with stable semantic field names. These are not wire names.
conventions.fixture_resolution: A fixture is either a full state or {extends, patch}. Patches use JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396): objects merge, arrays and scalars replace, null deletes.
conventions.given: state = merge(fixture state, vector.given). An absent given means the fixture unchanged.
conventions.record_defaults: Each record is merged over defaults.record, so a vector states only what differs.
conventions.expect_committed: state' = merge(state, expect.patch), plus the implied effects below.
conventions.implied_on_commit: Every committed record sets line.head_seq = head_seq + 1 and line.head_time = seq_time. Patches omit these two fields.
conventions.expect_rejected_or_noop: state' = state exactly. The durable outcome entry lives in the sequencer's outcome index, which is outside apply and is exercised by the traces.
conventions.sets: Sets are written as sorted arrays.
conventions.time: Integers in milliseconds on an abstract sequencer clock.
conventions.derived_floor: floor = the participant who did not write the last turn.
conventions.derived_status: status = lifecycle if lifecycle != open; else resolved if byes holds both participants; else open.
conventions.derived_entitled_readers: Credentials with reader == true and revoked == false.
conventions.payload_bearing_note: actor_declare is payload-bearing only when label == true. Every other type carries no line-scope ciphertext.
conventions.counter_domain: Every counter, sequence number and time is an integer in [0, 9007199254740991] (2^53-1), the safe-integer limit for consumers that read numbers as 64-bit binary floating point. Nothing wraps: a record that would advance a counter past the maximum is rejected exhausted and changes nothing.
rejection_precedence: unauthorized (origin: binding, declaration capability or capacity, current ownership, role)
conflict (identifier or key collision, or expect.*)
invalid (state-dependent: well-formed but wrong against current state)
exhausted (only for a record that would otherwise commit)
conventions.key_registry: Keys are opaque strings, each standing for an algorithm identifier and that algorithm's one accepted public encoding. A key that has held any role is reserved for life: line.root_key, every key in line.operators or line.tombstones.operator_keys, and both keys of every entry in line.credentials, revoked entries included. Reuse in any role is conflict.
conventions.absent_expectation: An expectation a record type requires and the record does not state is malformed (invalid, syntactic). It is never read as an expectation of 0, which is a real expected value.
conventions.operation_identity: (line, generation, signing principal, seen_seq, op_id). The principal is tagged by role: a credential, an operator key, or the root. Actor and credential origins share the credential's identity space. An op_id is unique only within its anchor. An anchor's whole identity space retires when the time floor is strictly greater than seq_time(seen_seq) + validity_max; only then may its hot entries be discarded. validity_max is fixed for a generation.
conventions.validity: The effective deadline is seq_time(seen_seq) + min(claimed validity, validity_max). The boundary is inclusive: evaluation exactly at the deadline is admissible.
conventions.rejection_precedence_scope: New admitted operations only. Admission errors and outcomes found by dedup lookup are outside the ladder.
conventions.namespace_capacity: actor_limit is the maximum number of live actors in the granted namespace, whichever credential holds them. An imported actor keeps its own namespace and does not count against the destination.
conventions.violation: Outcome of a sequencer-assigned value that no honest sequencer produces. A replaying client stops and reports it; it is not a rejection of an intent.

premises.decoded: The record decoded within bounds; no unknown version, field or scope.
premises.signature_verified: Stage 2 passed. Signatures are abstract here.
premises.admitted: Stage 4 passed: credential enrolled and unrevoked, generation current, anchor on accepted history, within validity. Admission is exercised by the traces, not by apply vectors.
premises.wraps_well_formed: A manifest's wrap commitments are present and well-formed. Whether a wrap decrypts is not checkable by the sequencer and is not modelled.
premises.typed_sequencer_path: The record is sequencer-origin. It carries no signature and was not admitted as an intent; it arrived over authenticated relay transport and takes the typed verification path of section 2 stage 2.
premises.root_signature_verified: The record is root-origin and its root signature verified. Root keys and proofs are abstract here.
premises.bootstrap_exempt: The record is line_init: it has no prior checkpoint and is exempt from validity (section 4.4). It replaces the admitted premise.
premises.replay_validation: The vector checks a sequencer-assigned value as a replaying client would. A violation here is evidence against the sequencer, not a rejection of the signed intent the record carries.
premises.size_class: Sizes are abstract: within_inline_limit or over_inline_limit. The numeric profile is a discussion value.
premises.derivation_abstract: A credential identifier is the derivation of the credential's two public keys. The derivation is a hash and is not computed here. A record states cred_id_mismatch: true when its identifier is not that derivation; otherwise it is taken to be.

traces.title: Sequencer clock faults
traces.note: How a discontinuity or a freeze is detected is deployment-specific. These steps state the premise (detected or not) and invent no threshold.

steps.do: premise: one day legitimately elapses with no traffic; an intent anchored before the idle period is then submitted
steps.expect: expired; an honest refusal; there is no cap on the forward step between commits

steps.do: premise: the sequencer detects a forward jump of one day that is not elapsed time; intents are pending
steps.expect: new authoritative evaluations and expiry-based compaction are suspended; nothing is expired by the jump; unresolved operations stay unresolved; an authorized historical receipt lookup still answers

steps.do: premise: the clock freezes at T and the fault is detected
steps.expect: evaluation is suspended as above

steps.do: premise: the clock freezes at T and the fault is not detected, or the sequencer is malicious; intents keep arriving
steps.expect: no intent expires by time and no real-time expiry guarantee holds; no operation that already has an outcome is re-evaluated; seq_time never decreases

steps.do: the sequencer restarts with a clock earlier than the persisted time floor
steps.expect: evaluation and expiry-based compaction are suspended; an authorized historical receipt lookup still answers; the time floor does not decrease
